as_told.title: Doc Brown modeled on Townsend Brown, per his daughter

plain: Podcast host Jesse Michels says that Doc Brown, the inventor in the 1985 film Back to the Future, was a nod to Townsend Brown, a real scientist who experimented with capacitors, devices that store electric charge, as a way to make things move. Michels points out that the film is set in 1985, the year Townsend Brown died, that the character's full name is Emmett Brown, that the film's "flux capacitor" echoes Brown's capacitor experiments, and that people called the real man "Doc Brown"; he links it to Steven Spielberg, who was behind the film, and says Brown's daughter told him directly she is sure the character is based on her father. If true, it would mean Hollywood quietly honored a little-known scientist tied to talk of anti-gravity.
